# Higher-dimensional MDS teaching examples

This is a selected, self-contained teaching subset of the completed
GRIP-EXP-039 study (29 September 2026), extracted on 2 October 2026.
It is separate from the original study archive and does not replace it.

## Selection and contents

Four target datasets: the data-seed-17 paraboloid with ambient distances and
with symmetric six-nearest-neighbor graph-path distances, HB/illc1033, and
HB/lock_700. The examples were selected after examining the experiment to
illustrate different distance targets and contrasting outcomes, not to estimate
success rates. All figures use optimizer start 17. Numerical tables retain
starts 17, 29, and 43; classical MDS is included once per target.

`examples.rds` contains original graph edges, lengths, vertex identities,
component membership, generating coordinates where available, and the two
small synthetic target matrices. Sixty saved three-column coordinate matrices
cover direct 3D MDS, classical MDS, classical-initialized 3D MDS, and PCA-only
and freely refined 3D results for intermediate dimensions 4, 6, 8, 10, 15, 20.
Scores include the corresponding higher-dimensional fits. The before-projection
coordinates themselves are not needed for these 3D views and are not included.
There are 244 original score rows and 72 corrected time-comparison rows.

No fit, coordinate scaling, input repair, or timing measurement occurs during
extraction. `source-hashes.csv` lists each imported source's relative path,
byte count and SHA-256 identity checked against the study evidence manifest.
The builder independently recomputes full uniform normalized stress for all
60 saved 3D configurations before saving the bundle. RDS version 2 with xz
compression is used; a round-trip identity check is mandatory.

Synthetic points sample a unit parameter disk and use z=x^2+y^2, generated by
dgraphs' quadform sampler. Graphs use symmetric nearest neighbors, Euclidean
edge lengths and component-MST repair. The ambient fixture retains the local
graph as ancillary geometry, but its distance matrix is ambient Euclidean;
the vignette draws no edges for that target.

## Algorithms and timing

The original study used full uniform SGD, dimensions 4–20, and three starts
for 51 target datasets. Its timing-instrumented wrapper was checked against
the package API during the study. It fits disconnected components separately,
centers and adjusts scale, and retains original-unit target distances.
Synthetic stages use 20 passes; gallery stages use four. This is bounded
optimization, not converged or globally optimal MDS.

Scores are sum of squared distance residuals divided by sum of squared finite
target distances. Cross-component pairs are excluded. The reported value is
not its square root. No additional scale is fitted when scoring saved PCA or
refined coordinates. View alignment/isolated-vertex placement affects only
presentation, not this evidence.

Route times include initialization, higher-dimensional fitting and PCA,
plus the free-coordinate stage where applicable. Shared preparation and
subsequent evaluation/rendering are excluded. Some wrapper archival overhead
is included. Corrected matched-time comparisons retain the best independently
scored direct checkpoint available within each route's charged budget;
checkpoint coordinates were not saved. Direct continuation omitted some
archival writes, giving it a conservatively generous allowance. The runs were
not a clean idle-machine kernel benchmark. The runnable public-API recipe in
the vignette is a separate illustration, not a remeasurement of these times.

## Attribution

Synthetic fixtures and original study results: Pawel Gajer / grip project.
SuiteSparse-derived graph data retain CC BY 4.0 attribution separately from
the package's GPL software license. HB/illc1033 is represented as a bipartite
row/column graph; HB/lock_700 uses symmetric off-diagonal nonzero support.
All edges have unit length. The installed `suitesparse.graph()` objects retain
full original contributor headers; see `inst/extdata/suitesparse/PROVENANCE.md`
and those objects' `provenance$source_header` fields. These graph conversions
and layouts are modifications of the original matrices. Cite Davis and Hu
(2011), *The University of Florida Sparse Matrix Collection*, ACM TOMS 38(1),
Article 1, DOI 10.1145/2049662.2049663.

## Rebuild

From a grip checkout, run:

```
Rscript data-raw/build-high-dimensional-mds.R /path/to/high_dimensional_mds_to_3d
make high-dimensional-vignette
```

The extraction needs the retained study archive, jsonlite and digest. It never
downloads or fits data. Rendering needs no study archive; the only new fits
are the small public-API demonstration. Install ivue and rgl for all four
interactive figures. Without them, the vignette keeps text and tables and
reports that interactive views are unavailable; it draws no static fallback.
